newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill spots close up, repo rates down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill spots close up, repo rates down.

text.p: Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Thursday despite the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, indicating investor confidence in a smooth leadership transition, traders siad.
Some traders said the negative impact of Deng's death was unlikely to be offset in just one day and any signs of instability would hit the state debt spot market hardest.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.77 million lots from 2.11 million on Wednesday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The most active three-year bond that matures in Aug 1999, a market barometer, rose to 104.28 yuan from 104.10 yuan.
The market opened mostly down on Deng's death but bargain-hunting quickly set in to push up prices, traders said.
"Deng's death caused a brief fall on the markets but confidence of a smooth transition of power helped prices go up for the rest of session," said one trader.

"But the negative impact has not been fully digested," he added. "If there is any sign of social instability, the spot market will be hit hardest because it is closely related to macro-economic activity."
Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Thursday with a short break in domestic A share issues reducing demand on the repo markets, traders said.
Trading was more active because sharp fluctuations on the stock markets due to Deng's death created more opportunities for speculative trading, traders said.
The most active three-day contract fell to 7.7 percent from nine percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover rose to 5.71 million lots from 3.43 million.
Traders said the stock market performance would be a key factor in any movement in the repo rates in the short-term.
